message.content: Pizza originated in **Naples, Italy**. In the late‑18th century, Neapolitan street vendors began topping thin dough with fresh tomatoes, olive oil, garlic, oregano, basil, and mozzarella cheese—ingredients locally available at the time. These early “pizza” were sold on the streets and quickly became popular among working people. Over the centuries, variations spread throughout Italy (e.g., Roman-style thicker crusts) and eventually around the world, evolving into countless regional styles while retaining their Italian roots.
